messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Serbian (Latin script), guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Serbian (Latin script) line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word/Phrase | Back‑Translation (EN) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|--------------------|------------------------|--------| | così | adverb (temporal/causal) – marks result | **tako** | “so / thus” | OK | | l'animo | noun, masc. sing., “the soul” (subject) | **duh** | “soul” | OK | | mio | possessive adjective – “my” | **moj** | “my” | OK | | ch'ancor | relative pronoun + adverb “which still” | **koji još** | “which still” | OK | | fuggiva | imperfect verb “was fleeing / flying” | **leteo** | “was flying” | OK | | si | reflexive clitic pronoun | **se** | (reflexive marker) | OK | | volse | remote past verb “turned” | **okrenuo** | “turned” | OK | | a (1st) | preposition introducing direction “to” (in *a retro*) | **nazad** (part of phrase) | “backward” | **UNNECESSARY** (Serbian does not need this preposition) | | retro | noun used adverbially “back” | **nazad** (part of phrase) | “back” | OK | | a (2nd) | preposition introducing infinitive purpose | **da** | “to” (infinitive marker) | OK | | rimirar | infinitive verb “to look again” | **pogleda** | “looks / to look” | OK | | lo | definite article (masc.) – not expressed in Serbian | — | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | passo | noun “pass” (direct object) | **prolaz** | “pass” | OK | | che (line 27) | relative pronoun “which” | **koji** | “which” | OK | | non | negation particle “not” (combined with *mai*) | **nikada** (part of negation) | “never” | OK | | lasciò | remote past verb “left” | **napustila** | “left / abandoned” | OK | | già | adverb “already” (temporal intensifier) | — | (none) | **MISSING** | | mai | adverb “never” (intensifier) | — (covered by *nikada*) | (none) | **UNNECESSARY** | | persona | noun “person” (feminine) | **osoba** | “person” | OK | | viva | adjective “living” (agreeing with *persona*) | **živa** | “living” | OK |

### Issues Summary - **MISSING**: *già* (the adverb “already” is not rendered in the Serbian translation). - **UNNECESSARY**: *a* (first occurrence) – Serbian does not require a preposition before *nazad*; *lo* – definite article omitted naturally; *mai* – its meaning is already captured by *nikada*. - **GRAMMAR**: none detected. - **WRONG**: none detected.

### Step 4: Correction & Final Output Fix any MISSING, WRONG, or GRAMMAR items from Step 3. Reorder within line if needed; do not add new content words. Verify that the output contains only Serbian (Latin script) script; no other language scripts should be mixed in. Output format (use nested bullet list, not table): - Line N: - Original: ... - Issue: ... (or "none") - Corrected: ... (or "no change") Output final Serbian (Latin script) text in ONE code block, line by line (no extra prose).
